Hello.

My name is Boomerang, and I've got a son. He is a little over 5 years old now, and has started to be unable to play all the new games the other kids are playing. He sometimes even freezes when I wake him up in the morning, forcing me to .. .. hard reset him.. okay I ran out of analogies.

So, my computer is old af and I think it's dying on me. When I'm buying a new PC, should I try and salvage any parts of the old PC (not talking peripherals)? For example the drives, I've got both SSD and harddrives. Should I salvage them?
New computer: Salvage any part of old PC or go all new parts?

Depends... Drives, case parts (fans) and peripherals can last for years... I personally don't skimp on any of those three, expecting to use them for some time. The rest is bound to the motherboard. New board is new plug for chip, new plug for memory, new plug for power on occasion... Much of what is in the computer isn't worth salvaging.
If it's even sorta power friendly components, it may make for a nice network device. However power alone would outdate many devices. Having a home network server wasting a couple hundred watts will cost more than a prosperously designed machine.
EDIT: I like to use a common reference for older parts... If it's slower than the $35 raspberry pi, why isn't it replaced with a $35 board that uses half the power. Not that the raspberry pi is good, but it's cheap and fairly common.

I personally believe if you just need normal components, it will be cheaper to wait for a special offer where a complete system has all you need (and some extras) than to buy the parts. As you seem to have time, I suggest waiting for a very good deal.

In the meantime, a fresh install of your os, or taking out unnecessary parts, can help you pin down what part causes the freezing. Linux can be installed on any (even external) drive and may also run faster on your old machine - good for testing the hardware and trying out what that can do, and you can still run Windows on your main drive.

After you got the new one, you may keep the old one for compatibility with old games and other programs, for playing around, as backup, or such. Unnecessary components can be removed and used for both computers if still suitable. The hdd for instance can be put in an external case if necessary, and used for data storage (backups) on both machines, if it's big enough and still works well.
